metadata.note: The Great Northern's route east from Great Falls across the Judith Basin -- Armington, Belt, Stanford, Moccasin -- and then south on the Moccasin-Lewistown branch of 1912. One pair of trains, the Judith Special, worked it through from Great Falls to Lewistown. It was the last passenger service into Great Falls of any kind, ending in 1966, five years after the Havre-Butte trains and eleven after the Milwaukee Road's. The Great Falls-Moccasin portion is the northern end of the Great Northern's Great Falls-Judith Gap-Billings line and is still busy BNSF freight track; freight-only years are not drawn (CLAUDE.md Rule 1).

metadata.not_yet_sourced: The end year, 1966, and the train name "Judith Special" both rest on a single roadside marker that could not be fetched directly (hmdb.org served a Cloudflare challenge); both were read as search-engine quotations of it. Treat them as unconfirmed. The opening date of the Great Falls-Moccasin line itself -- the Great Northern's Billings line, built by the Billings and Northern in the late 1900s -- was not sourced, so this feature starts in 1913 with the Lewistown branch rather than at whatever earlier date Great Falls-Moccasin trains began. Headways, speed and the 1955 segment boundary are estimates or editorial. Intermediate stations were not compiled.
geometry_sources: Traced on real track in OpenStreetMap by corridor-constrained Dijkstra over every railway=rail/abandoned/disused/razed way in the corridor, between OSM place nodes; simplified Douglas-Peucker at 40 m. No straight-line approximations beyond the sub-kilometre bridges noted per feature.

Overpass API (maps.mail.ru mirror), bbox dump of every railway way between Great Falls, Stanford, Moccasin and Lewistown, pulled 2026-08-26; corridor waypoints Armington, Belt, Stanford, Windham, Moccasin. Endpoints are the OSM place nodes for Great Falls and Lewistown.

Fit: 189.5 km traced vs about 118 documented miles (190 km), 1.00x. Composition: 128.9 km BNSF Laurel Subdivision (old_railway_operator=GN), 33.1 km Central Montana Rail, the rest untagged track and abandoned grade.

properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced. 189.5 km (117.8 mi) against roughly 118 miles for Great Falls–Moccasin–Lewistown (about 98 miles to Moccasin plus the documented 19.6-mile branch), a 1.00x match. 128.9 km of it runs on today's BNSF Laurel Subdivision, tagged old_railway_operator=GN in OSM, and 33.1 km on Central Montana Rail. Largest straight-line bridge 0.92 km; endpoints snapped 0.96 km (Great Falls) and 0.44 km (Lewistown) from their OSM place nodes.

segments.note: The Great Northern reached Lewistown from the west in 1912-13, building a branch south from Moccasin on its Great Falls-Judith Gap-Billings line; the branch was completed on Nov 20 1912. One pair of trains, the Judith Special, ran through from Great Falls to Lewistown over the two together. Frequency estimated, unsourced
